skill.name: gdpr-data-handling
skill.description: Build GDPR-compliant data handling workflows for consent, DSARs, retention, privacy by design, and breach notification.
skill.summary: Guide GDPR implementation for consent, data subject rights, retention, privacy by design, and breach response.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, documentation links, abstract database examples, and ordinary GDPR terminology. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. The DSAR examples omit verification and ownership checks before returning, deleting, or exporting personal data.

remediation.issue: DSAR processing examples do not enforce requester verification before data access, erasure, or portability actions.
remediation.suggestion: Add checks for verified status, authenticated requester identity, request ownership, workflow state, and audit logging before any personal data operation.

remediation.issue: Example DSAR methods act on a request_id alone.
remediation.suggestion: Bind each request to a user and session context, and reject operations when the caller cannot prove authorization for that subject.

semantic_findings.title: DSAR Processing Lacks Verification Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: The DSAR examples accept a verified flag during request submission. Processing functions then retrieve by request_id and return, delete, or export personal data without authorization checks. A leaked or guessed request ID could expose or erase personal data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly records verification state when creating a request, then processes access, erasure, and portability paths without checking that state. This is a clear privacy authorization gap in the example workflow.

content.value_statement: GDPR systems need clear consent, rights, retention, and breach workflows. This skill gives practical patterns for privacy-focused implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Explains GDPR personal data categories and lawful bases.
Provides consent management data models and user interface patterns.
Shows DSAR workflows for access, erasure, and portability requests.
Defines retention policy examples with deletion and anonymization paths.
Outlines privacy by design data models and data minimization checks.
Lists breach notification steps and GDPR implementation checklist items.
limitations: It is guidance, not legal advice for a specific jurisdiction or controller.
Code snippets are examples and need authentication, authorization, and production hardening.
It does not connect to live systems or verify a real organization.
External GDPR links may change and should be checked before use.

use_cases.title: Design Consent Controls
use_cases.description: Create consent categories, preference flows, and audit records for products that process EU personal data.

use_cases.title: Build DSAR Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan access, erasure, rectification, and portability processes with deadlines, exceptions, and response records.

use_cases.title: Review GDPR Readiness
use_cases.description: Check retention, privacy by design, breach response, and documentation against common GDPR implementation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Map Personal Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gdpr-data-handling to identify personal data categories, lawful bases, and protection levels for this product: [describe product].

prompt_templates.title: Design Consent Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gdpr-data-handling to design a consent model and preference flow for [application]. Include audit history and withdrawal handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan DSAR Fulfillment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gdpr-data-handling to create an access, erasure, and portability workflow for [system]. Include verification, deadlines, exceptions, and audit logs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Privacy Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gdpr-data-handling to review this architecture for GDPR privacy by design, retention, minimization, breach response, and transfer safeguards: [details].

output_examples.input: A SaaS app needs analytics consent before tracking EU visitors.
output_examples.output: A consent plan separates necessary and analytics categories, records policy version and timestamp, and provides reject and save options.

output_examples.input: A user requests deletion of all account data.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines verification, legal retention checks, deletion across sources, exception records, and completion logging within the GDPR deadline.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce stored behavioral data.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends purpose-based retention periods, anonymization of old analytics, and documentation of deletion actions.

best_practices: Verify requester identity before any DSAR access, erasure, or portability action.
Separate consent purposes and record each change with timestamp and policy version.
Define retention periods for each data type and automate deletion or anonymization.
anti_patterns: Using pre-selected consent boxes or bundling unrelated purposes together.
Returning personal data from a DSAR workflow before authorization checks finish.
Keeping personal data indefinitely because deletion rules are undocumented.

faq.question: Is this skill legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and should be reviewed by qualified privacy counsel.

faq.question: What GDPR areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers consent, data subject rights, retention, privacy by design, breach notification, and checklists.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides examples that need authentication, authorization, testing, and legal review before production use.

faq.question: Does it process live personal data?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a written guide and does not connect to live databases.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the marketplace metadata.

faq.question: What should I verify first?
faq.answer: Confirm legal bases, requester verification, retention duties, and jurisdiction-specific requirements.
